author.bio1: Jon Peciña is an Industrial Engineer (UNAV) with a Master's in Full Stack Development (UNIR) who converted to AI Engineering: he builds complete applications — frontend, backend, testing and DevOps — accelerated by AI tools.
author.bio2: After 22 years in corporate finance across Spain, the Netherlands and Peru, he now crafts web experiences that combine rigorous data work with polished interfaces.
author.bio3: Vidas de Santos was born from that mix: an exhaustive, data-driven index of more than two thousand saints, with live biographies served from Wikipedia and filters by country, religious order and century.
author.contactText: Questions, corrections or ideas for the index? Get in touch.
author.moreProjectsText: Explore his other builds: discovery portals, learning academies and browser games — all crafted with the same care.

history.p1: In the first centuries, saints were acclaimed by the people: martyrs who died for the faith and confessors whose heroic lives inspired devotion. There was no formal process — the sensus fidelium, the sense of the faithful, was enough.
history.p2: From the 10th century onward, popes began reserving canonizations to the Holy See. In 1588 Sixtus V created the Congregation of Rites, and in 1969 Paul VI reorganized it as the Congregation for the Causes of Saints, the dicastery that still examines every cause today.
history.p3: The modern path has four stages: Servant of God, Venerable, Blessed (after one verified miracle, or martyrdom) and Saint (after a second miracle). Each step requires a rigorous historical, theological and medical examination.
history.p4: This portal indexes the men and women — and a few groups — whom the Church, East and West, venerates as saints, alongside blesseds on their way to canonization. Biographies are served live from Wikipedia, which keeps them current.
history.title: From martyrdom to canonization

privacy.p1: Vidas de Santos runs entirely in your browser. There is no backend, no accounts and no tracking of individuals.
privacy.p2: We store only functional preferences on your device via localStorage: interface language, recently viewed saints and cached Wikipedia excerpts (24h). You can clear them anytime from your browser settings.
privacy.p3: Anonymous usage statistics are collected with Vercel Analytics to understand which pages are visited. No personal data is collected.
privacy.title: Privacy

sources.p1: The saint index was compiled from the English Wikipedia's list of Catholic saints and enriched with structured data from Wikidata (countries, dates, religious orders) plus curated lists such as the 37 Doctors of the Church.
sources.p2: Biographies are loaded on demand from Wikipedia (MediaWiki REST API and Action API) in Spanish when available, falling back to English. They are cached in your browser for 24 hours. All article content belongs to its Wikipedia authors and is available under CC BY-SA.
sources.p3: Portraits come from Wikimedia Commons via the Wikipedia API. This is an independent educational project, not affiliated with the Holy See, any diocese or religious order.
sources.title: Sources
